newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore dengue cases top 550 in November - paper.
newsitem.headline: Singapore dengue cases top 550 in November - paper.

text.p: A total of 551 dengue fever cases were reported in Singapore in November, the highest monthly total ever, the Straits Times newspaper said on Saturday.
The newspaper quoted the Environment Ministry as saying 2,575 dengue fever cases had been reported so far this year against 1,983 cases for all of 1995.

It also said the 551 cases reported in November was more than twice the number in the same month last year, but did give the November 1995 figure. It also did not specify what the previous high figure was for a single month.
But it said the situation was not expected to improve because of torrential rains hitting the city-state.

"We need the cooperation of residents, contractors and estate management officials to keep their premises free of mosquito breeding (areas)," an Environment Ministry spokesman told the newspaper. "We've also reinforced the dengue control workforce."
Dengue fever is caused by infected mosquitoes and is a particular problem during the rainy season in Singapore, which normally comes at the end of the year.
